Ben / team —

Thanks for the heads up and Olive’s notes. High level legal posture and recommended negotiating positions from Redwood Legal:

1) Controller/Processor: Redwood maintains a Processor posture for the services in the Order Form. If ODIN proposes Controller-to-Controller language, we need specific examples of downstream processing ODIN is concerned about; otherwise we should preserve Processor wording and add a limited "data use" exhibit.

2) SCCs/TIA: Accept EU SCCs (2021) with our standard TIA exhibit. We can accept the TIA but will limit the operational commitments to what we can guarantee (region routing for certain tenant-level flags only; not blanket contractual guarantees for all data types). See Redwood_DPA_playbook.pdf for fallback language.

3) Subprocessor cadence: Agree to quarterly disclosure plus emergency notifications. If ODIN insists on 30-day pre-notice we can offer a 30-day notice for planned subprocessors but need carveouts for emergency security patches.

4) Data localization/Export controls: We cannot commit to absolute EU-only routing for all data sets given multi-tenant infrastructure. Offer: a contractual routing escalation and an optional Dedicated deployment addendum (Dedicated GPU pools) as a commercial alternative if ODIN requires hard regional isolation.

5) Audit & evidence: Provide SOC2 and limited export-control evidence. Explicitly refuse unlimited audit windows — offer an annual on-site or virtual audit window (subject to NDAs and scope).

6) Signoff path: prioritize final DPA within two business days after redline closure, with DocuSign owner set to Ben (for Sales) and Laura (for legal).

I’m attaching the playbook and a short redline we can send as a counter (Redwood_DPA_playbook.pdf). If you want me on the call Tuesday — I can join the 11:00 PT slot.

Laura Bennett
